newsitem.title: INDIA: ANZ says cutting costs to foil predators.
newsitem.headline: ANZ says cutting costs to foil predators.

text.p: The Australia and New Zealand Banking Group Ltd (ANZ) is vigorously cutting costs to improve its performance and reinforce defences against takeover bids, Chairman Charles Goode said on Tuesday.
"Our profits have gone up quite well over the last few years, and we're making a real drive on costs," Goode told Reuters in an interview in New Delhi.
"So, we're going to get that (cost-to-income) ratio down."
Goode was responding to a question on the bank's apparent vulnerability to a takeover bid because of a cost-to-income ratio of 67.3 percent -- the highest among Australia's "Big Four" banks.
"Our defences are our good performance and our future prospects, including in countries like India," he said.

"We have told shareholders it will look better in this year's result and the results two or three years out, because we are going to get our costs down, and therefore, by our performance, we don't see ourselves as a sitting target."
Last November ANZ said net profit for the year to September 30, 1996 rose 6.7 percent to A$1.12 billion (US$869 million).
Goode, in New Delhi for a group board meeting, said ANZ planned to invest A$50 million in modernising and upgrading its Indian operations over the next three years.
ANZ has 56 branches in India, where it has been operating since the mid-19th century. It also runs a credit-card operation in India.
Mercer said on Monday ANZ had hired U.S. management consultant KPMG Barents to carry out a "process re-engineering" study.

"We are obviously in search of continuing cost efficiencies," he said. "There are synergies in information technology and management systems that will help us. For instance we run our Indian credit-card business out of Australia."

Both ANZ officials said the Wallis inquiry into Australia's financial system could well result in an end to the "six pillars" policy laid down by former Australian Prime Minister Paul Keating which banned mergers and takeovers among the country's four large banks and two major life insurers.
Stan Wallis, who chairs the financial system inquiry by Australian Treasurer Peter Costello, said earlier this month he expected his report to be ready by the end of March.

The inquiry has received submissions from the banking, financial and insurance sectors about changes to the regulatory framework, which now prevents mega-mergers between the major banks and life offices, and also frowns on takeovers of the regional banks that specialise in home loans.

Analysts have constantly pointed to the likelihood that National Australia Bank Ltd will launch a takeover of fellow "Big Four" bank Westpac Banking Corp once the Wallis report is handed down. (A$1 = US$0.776)
